comparison.a: Candidate A proposes a sequential, single-pipeline architecture (O1) with a big-bang milestone strategy. This approach maximizes determinism and simplicity at the cost of being the slowest option for execution.
comparison.b: Candidate B proposes a task-parallel architecture (O2) with a phased, hybrid milestone strategy. This aims for faster wall-clock time and de-risks the complex implementation by building the system incrementally.

evidence.note: Candidate A chose the simpler, sequential O1 architecture.
Candidate A uses a big-bang milestone strategy with a single linear pipeline.
evidence.quote: ...implements the Implementation Council as a sequential staged pipeline (O1) under a big-bang milestone strategy... The entire workflow—Intake → Work Planning → Generate → Validate → Review → Patch →

evidence.note: Candidate B chose the more complex but faster parallel O2 architecture.
Candidate B uses a phased milestone strategy to de-risk implementation, starting with a foundation.

payload.notes: Candidate B is superior. Its parallel architecture (O2) is a more practical solution for real-world throughput needs. More importantly, its hybrid, phased milestone strategy is a far more realistic and de-risked plan for implementing a complex system than Candidate A's rigid, all-or-nothing 'big-bang' approach.
